title: Primitivity of a tournament's adjacency matrix
statement: Let $D$ be a tournament on a finite vertex set $V$ (an orientation of the complete graph on $V$), and let $A$ be its $0/1$ adjacency matrix. Then $A$ is primitive — that is, some power $A^{k}$ has all entries positive — if and only if $D$ is diconnected (every vertex is reachable from every other) and $V$ has at least four vertices.
hypotheses_covered: D is a tournament (orientation of the complete graph)
A is the 0/1 adjacency matrix of D
conclusion: A primitive iff D diconnected and card V >= 4
